name: showcase_dam_break
_comment: Native PhysicsView port of the Blender crystal_sph_addon preset SHOWCASE_DAM_BREAK
converted from Blender's Z-up world space to PhysicsView's Y-up convention via
own default). Not run by run_physics_scenarios.ps1's default sweep -- it only
globs scenarios/*.json directly, not subdirectories -- because this is an 800k-
particle, 4800-physics-step bake (minutes, not the seconds a regression scenario
should take), not a fast pass/fail check. Run explicitly:
Known simplification vs. the addon preset: the two pillar/step obstacles that
split the collapsing column into three jets are NOT ported. The addon represents
them as extra is_static=true SPH particles baked into the same fluid, a Python-
side technique with no equivalent on the native FluidWorld/WCSPHFluid model (a
single fluid, single particle set). The dam-break collapse itself -- this scene's
actual physics content -- is otherwise a faithful port.

steps.label: WCSPH (only solver the showcase presets use)
preset doesn't override pressure_coe_scale -> addon default 1.96
no extra source regions (single box via SetFluidBounds above is enough for this preset)
no sphere boundary in this preset
rebuild fluid with the above params
precondition: ~800k particles from the 0.36x0.56x0.48m column at 5mm spacing
bake 240 frames x 20 substeps = 4800 physics steps (1 frame = 20*2.5e-4 = 5ms physical time), one PLY per frame
invariant: particle count conserved (no emitter/outflow in this preset)
